newsitem.title: USA: Ply Gem says plans to end Atrium merger.
newsitem.headline: Ply Gem says plans to end Atrium merger.

text.p: Ply Gem Industries Inc said Monday that it has notified Atrium Corp of its intention to terminate their merger agreement in order to accept a higher bid from an undisclosed third party.
Last week, Ply Gem, a New York-based maker of home-improvement products including replacement windows and siding, said it received a $19.50 per share bid from an unnamed party.
The offer rivals Atrium's $18.75 per share bid, or a total of $482 million, that was first announced in late June.
Atrium is 80 percent owned by buyout firm Hicks, Muse, Tate & Furst Inc. Both Atrium and Hicks, Muse are private.

Termination of the Atrium agreement "will be effective only if Ply Gem gives an actual notice on July 24. In the interim, Ply Gem is obligated to consider any revised proposal that Atrium may elect to make," Ply Gem said in a statement.

The unnamed bidder has advised Ply Gem that it has a portion of the funds for the transaction, and has arranged a bridge financing commitment letter from a financial institution to secure the remaining funds, the statement said.
Any tender offer for Ply Gem from the new bidder would be subject to "receipt of the funds contemplated by the bridge commitment letter" among other conditions.
If Ply Gem ends the Atrium deal, it will be obligated to pay Atrium a $9.5 million fee and to reimburse Atrium for up to $2.5 million of expenses.
The new bidder would fund these amounts by buying 640,000 shares of PLY GEM stock, at a price of $18.75 per share, for a total investment of $12 million, Ply Gem said in its statement.
